absent: Execution harness that interprets flags, expected outcomes, and repeat counts
Internals of generation routines referenced by entries
Verifier and just-in-time conversion rules for branches
Full instruction encoding, register file, and flag definitions

findings.text: Entries in this catalog share a common record shape. Each has a descriptive label, a way to obtain instructions either inline or from a generation routine, category flags, expected outcomes for execution classes, and optional needs for stack space or repeated runs.

Sixty-four-bit load-immediate entries exercise combinations of byte polarity. Separate entries cover checker output, positive mixed with zero, negative mixed with zero, and positive mixed with negative, all treated as internal cases without input data.

Atomic updates are tested at two widths across arithmetic, bitwise, fetch-augmented, exchange, and compare-exchange forms. One group varies register pairing for each operation while requesting a small stack area and expecting success for the exercised class.

A second atomic group varies operand magnitudes rather than registers. It repeats execution many times under a shared pattern-run count, again at both widths and across the same family of update forms, with internal handling and no input data.

Conditional branches are swept over immediate and register magnitudes in both full and thirty-two-bit forms. Coverage spans equality, bit-set, and unsigned plus signed ordering conditions, each generated per condition and repeated over pattern runs without input data.

Some branch entries encode statically known outcomes. Boundary immediates such as all-clear, all-set, and signed extremes produce always-taken or never-taken behavior, and comparisons of a register against itself yield the fixed result implied by each condition, verified through expected return values.

Short forward jumps check small offsets from zero through four. Each case starts from a cleared result, uses an equality test that is satisfied, skips a matching number of increment steps, and expects a cleared outcome, with verifier zero-extension handling requested.

Long conditional jumps distinguish runtime decisions from conversions known during just-in-time processing. Separate generated cases cover taken at runtime, not taken at runtime, always taken, and never taken for the thirty-two-bit form, distinguished by expected return codes.
Atomic register-pair and magnitude entries declare a stack requirement of eight units.

Most entries in this slice expect outcome zero for the first class and one for the second, while constant-decision and long-jump cases vary the second value among zero, one, and two to encode never-taken, taken, or fall-through paths.
